mergedParams.userDescription: Pixelated, 8-bit style text, soft, muted colors, and rigid movement. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: 8-Bit Pixelated Text with Muted Colors & Rigid Motion

prompts.prompt: Create a pixelated 8-bit style typography preset that mimics classic arcade game text animations. Think of how text appears in retro games - letter by letter with a sharp, blocky reveal effect. Each letter should snap into place with rigid, non-interpolated movement (no smooth transitions). Use a stepped timing function to create that authentic 8-bit feel where positions update in discrete jumps rather than fluid motion. The text should have a subtle pixel-perfect outline effect using text-shadow, and colors should be desaturated pastels (like faded arcade cabinet screens). Add a gentle CRT-style scanline overlay that moves vertically across the text. When words appear, they should 'type out' character by character with a mechanical rhythm, followed by a brief flash/blink effect like old computer terminals. Consider adding a subtle chromatic aberration effect on emphasis words by offsetting RGB channels slightly.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Use BaseLayout with 'relative overflow-hidden' for the main container. For typography, use TextAtom components with caption data for word-level timing. Apply 'font-mono' class for monospace font. Create pixelated effect using CSS image-rendering: pixelated on a scaled-down then scaled-up text layer. Use transform: translateX/Y with steps() timing function for rigid movement. Add scanline effect as a ::before pseudo-element with 'absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none' and linear gradient background. Implement chromatic aberration using multiple text-shadow layers with red/cyan offsets. Use generic keyframe effects with easing: 'steps(8, end)' for authentic 8-bit motion. Set up word reveals using opacity effects with ranges based on caption word timing. Colors: Use CSS custom properties for muted palette (#8B956D, #C4CFA1, #6B7353). Performance: Use will-change: transform on moving elements, GPU-accelerated transforms only.

prompts.prompt: Design a glitchy pixel art typography preset inspired by corrupted NES graphics and datamoshing effects. Imagine the text as if it's being displayed on a failing CRT monitor with memory corruption. The base text should be rendered in chunky pixel fonts, but periodically 'glitch out' with horizontal displacement bars, color channel separation, and pixel sorting effects. During glitch moments, random characters should briefly transform into different symbols or scramble their positions. Implement a 'bad signal' effect where the text occasionally shifts horizontally with tearing artifacts. Colors should alternate between muted retro palettes and sudden bursts of oversaturated glitch colors (hot pinks, electric blues) during corruption events. Add digital noise patterns that intensify during transitions. The overall movement should feel mechanical and quantized, like the text is locked to an invisible grid system.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gray-900' as base. Create multiple TextAtom layers for glitch effects. Main text uses 'font-mono text-4xl' with custom pixel font. Implement glitch bars using absolutely positioned divs with 'h-1 w-full mix-blend-screen' and random translateX animations. Use clip-path: inset() for tearing effects. Apply SVG filters for pixel sorting and displacement mapping. Create scramble effect by swapping textContent in rapid succession using caption data indices. Use internal effect presets for reusable glitch patterns. Set up waveform effects if audio is present to trigger glitches on beats. Color channels: Use CSS filters hue-rotate() and saturate() with keyframe animations. Grid snapping: Round all translate values to nearest 8px increment. Timing: Use AnimationRange with random delays between 100-500ms for glitch triggers. Performance: Batch DOM updates, use transform3d() for hardware acceleration.

prompts.prompt: Build a Game Boy-inspired kinetic typography preset with authentic 4-color palette limitations and tile-based movement system. Visualize text as if it's rendered on the original Game Boy's LCD screen with its characteristic green monochrome display and visible pixel grid. Each word should slide in from off-screen edges in strict 8-pixel increments, mimicking sprite movement in Game Boy games. Implement the classic 'ghosting' effect where previous positions leave faint trails that quickly fade. Text should pulse with a subtle backlight flicker effect. For emphasis words, create a 'power-up' animation where the text briefly inverts colors and scales up in pixelated steps. Add dot matrix printer-style reveal for longer sentences, where text scrolls horizontally with a typewriter effect. Include subtle LCD refresh artifacts where pixels take a moment to fully transition between states.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative bg-green-950 overflow-hidden' container. Apply custom CSS filter for Game Boy palette (#0f380f, #306230, #8bac0f, #9bbc0f). Use grid layout with 'grid-cols-20 grid-rows-18' to enforce tile-based positioning. TextAtom components with 'font-mono text-2xl' for pixel perfect alignment. Create ghosting with multiple opacity layers at transform offsets, each with 'absolute opacity-20'. Implement movement using transform: translate() with calc() based on grid units (8px). LCD artifacts: Use mix-blend-mode: multiply with animated opacity. Flicker effect: Subtle brightness filter animation at 60fps. Power-up animation: Scale transform with steps(3) timing, combined with filter: invert(). Typewriter reveal: Use overflow: hidden with animated width based on caption timing. All animations use steps() easing for authentic retro feel. FitDurationTo: 'children' to match caption length.

prompts.prompt: Create a terminal-based hacker aesthetic typography preset with 8-bit ASCII art influences and command-line interface animations. Picture text appearing as if typed on an old phosphor terminal with green or amber monochrome display. Each word should 'compile' into view with a cascade of random characters that resolve into the final text, like a decryption sequence. Add authentic terminal features: blinking cursor, scan lines, phosphor bloom on bright text, and occasional 'buffer overflow' where text briefly corrupts. Implement a matrix-rain effect in the background with falling ASCII characters. For important words, trigger a 'system alert' animation with flashing borders made of box-drawing characters. Include random 'lag spikes' where animation freezes momentarily, simulating low-performance hardware. Colors should be limited to terminal green/amber with subtle glow effects.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'bg-black relative font-mono overflow-hidden' base. Background matrix rain: Separate BaseLayout with 'absolute inset-0 opacity-30' containing multiple columns of falling TextAtom components with random ASCII characters. Main text container: 'relative z-10 p-8'. Decryption effect: Use caption data to progressively reveal words, with each word starting as random characters that swap rapidly (setInterval 50ms) before resolving. Cursor: ::after pseudo-element with 'inline-block w-2 h-5 bg-green-400 animate-pulse'. Phosphor bloom: text-shadow with multiple green layers (0 0 10px #00ff00). Scan lines: CSS gradient overlay with animation. Box borders: Use Unicode box-drawing characters (═║╔╗╚╝) in separate TextAtoms positioned absolutely. Lag spikes: Randomly pause all animations using animation-play-state. Use internal effect presets for terminal glow and scanline effects. Performance: Use CSS containment for matrix rain columns.

prompts.prompt: Develop a sprite-sheet inspired kinetic typography where text behaves like 2D platformer game characters with physics-based movement. Each word should act as an individual sprite with idle animations (subtle bobbing), jump movements with gravity, and landing impacts. Implement pixel-perfect collision detection where words 'land' on invisible platforms at different heights. When new words enter, they should 'spawn' with a classic teleportation effect (vertical light beam or sparkle pixels). Important words perform special moves like double-jumps or spin attacks. Add retro particle effects using single pixels that emit when words move. Colors follow NES palette limitations with dithering patterns for gradients. Include power-up transformations where words temporarily gain new abilities (faster movement, trailing shadows, size changes). Background should have parallax scrolling pixel clouds or geometric patterns.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout structure with multiple layers for parallax: 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Each word as separate BaseLayout with 'absolute' positioning. Implement gravity using quadratic easing in translateY animations. Jump arc: Combine translateY (parabolic) with translateX (linear). Use caption timing to trigger word spawns. Idle animation: Small translateY oscillation with sin() easing. Landing impact: Scale bounce animation (1 → 0.8 → 1.1 → 1). Particle system: Multiple small divs with 'absolute w-1 h-1 bg-white' animated outward. Collision detection: Calculate landing positions based on word index and preset platforms array. Teleport effect: Vertical gradient div with opacity fade. Use repeatChildrenProps for consistent word behavior. Power-ups: Switch between internal effect presets based on caption metadata. Dithering: CSS background-image with repeating pixel patterns. Performance: Use transform3d(), limit particle count, batch animations.

prompts.prompt: Design a retro computer boot sequence typography preset that mimics BIOS and DOS startup screens with rigid, monospace text rendering. Text should appear line by line with authentic computer boot timing - system checks, memory counting, driver loading messages interspersed with the actual content. Each line types out character by character at varying speeds (faster for 'system' text, slower for content). Include classic computer UI elements: ASCII progress bars that fill as text loads, blinking status indicators (OK/FAIL), memory address counters in hexadecimal. Add CRT monitor effects: subtle screen curvature distortion, phosphor persistence, electromagnetic interference waves. For emphasis words, trigger a 'CRITICAL ERROR' style alert with red flashing background and beeping sound effect visualization. Implement random 'boot delays' where cursor blinks waiting for input. Colors limited to CGA palette with harsh contrast.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'bg-black text-green-400 font-mono p-4 relative' base. Structure text as series of divs each containing one line. Use flexbox 'flex-col gap-0' for line stacking. Character typing: Split caption data into characters, reveal using JavaScript with setTimeout delays (30-80ms random). ASCII progress bars: Use TextAtom with characters like [████░░░░]. Status indicators: Span elements with 'inline-block w-20' and conditional coloring. Memory counters: Separate TextAtom with incrementing hex values using setInterval. CRT effects: CSS transform: perspective() and rotateX() for curvature, multiple box-shadows for glow. Phosphor persistence: Previous text positions with decreasing opacity. Interference: Animated CSS filter: url(#turbulence) with SVG filter. Error alerts: Toggle 'bg-red-600 animate-pulse' class on container. Boot delays: Add empty AnimationRanges with no property changes. Use fitDurationTo: 'children' with added pause ranges.

prompts.prompt: Build a chunky isometric pixel art typography preset where text exists in a 3D pixelated space with dimetric projection. Each word should appear as a solid 3D block with visible top and side faces, rendered in pixel art style. Words stack and arrange themselves like Tetris blocks, falling into place with satisfying snap movements. Implement authentic pixel art shading with limited color ramps (3-4 shades per color). Add construction animation where words build up pixel by pixel from bottom to top, like a 3D printer. Include ambient animations: floating pixel dust, subtle breathing scaling, occasional pixel particles breaking off edges. For emphasis, words should rotate in isometric space showing all faces. Create depth with layer ordering and drop shadows. Movement uses integer pixel values only, no sub-pixel positioning. Color palette inspired by 16-bit era games with vibrant but limited selections.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative perspective-none' to maintain pixel precision. Each word as nested BaseLayouts: main container with 'relative', three faces as 'absolute' divs. Isometric transformation: transform: rotateX(30deg) rotateY(-45deg). Top face: 'bg-blue-400', right face: 'bg-blue-600', front face: 'bg-blue-500'. Pixel shading: Use linear-gradient with hard stops for pixel art shadows. Build animation: Clip-path animating from bottom (inset(100% 0 0 0)) to top (inset(0)). Falling motion: TranslateY with steps(10) easing, snap to grid positions (multiples of 16px). Pixel dust: Small absolutely positioned divs with 'w-2 h-2' floating via translateY. Breathing: Subtle scale animation (1 to 1.05). Rotation: Transform rotateY from -45deg to 315deg over 1s. Layer ordering: Use z-index based on word position. Drop shadows: Box-shadow with no blur (4px 4px 0 black). All positions rounded to nearest pixel. Use internal effects for consistent 3D transforms.

prompts.prompt: Create a vintage arcade cabinet screen typography preset with authentic CRT display characteristics and attract mode animations. Text should appear as if displayed on a curved arcade monitor with visible scanlines, color bleeding, and barrel distortion. Implement 'INSERT COIN' style flashing prompts between text segments. Each word enters with classic arcade game flourishes: point value pop-ups (+100, +500), combo multipliers, or bonus indicators. Add screen burn-in effects where frequently displayed text leaves ghost images. Include authentic arcade artifacts: phosphor bloom on bright colors, RGB convergence issues at screen edges, occasional static interference. For high-impact words, trigger 'HIGH SCORE' animations with rotating 3D text and particle celebrations. Background should have subtle scrolling starfield or geometric patterns. Colors use limited arcade palette with oversaturated primaries and characteristic color bleeding between pixels.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative overflow-hidden bg-gray-900 rounded-lg' for CRT shape. Apply CSS filter: contrast(1.1) brightness(1.2) for arcade look. Barrel distortion: Use transform: scale3d() with different values for center vs edges. Scanlines: ::before element with repeating linear gradient, 'absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none opacity-50'. Color bleeding: Multiple text-shadows with RGB offsets (red: -1px, blue: 1px). INSERT COIN: Separate TextAtom with 'animate-pulse text-yellow-400'. Point pop-ups: Absolutely positioned divs animating translateY(-20px) with fade out. Screen burn: Lower opacity duplicate layers with slight offset. Phosphor bloom: Layered text-shadows with decreasing opacity. RGB convergence: Use CSS filters or split color channels into separate layers. Static: Rapidly toggling noise pattern background. HIGH SCORE: 3D rotation using rotateY animation. Particles: Multiple small divs with radial burst animations. Starfield: Background layer with moving dot pattern. Use waveform effects to sync celebrations with audio beats if available.

prompts.prompt: Develop a pixel RPG dialogue box typography preset that mimics classic JRPG text systems with character portraits and menu-style borders. Text appears inside pixelated speech bubbles or dialogue boxes with 9-slice scaling borders made of repeated tile patterns. Implement character-by-character reveal with authentic typewriter sounds visualization (small bounce per character). Add emotion indicators: exclamation marks for surprise, ellipses for thinking, emotion bubbles with pixel icons. Include menu selection animations where certain words highlight with a moving cursor sprite. For dramatic moments, implement screen shake and flash effects. Text should respect box boundaries with automatic line breaks. Add subtle portrait animations: blinking, mouth movement synced with text speed. Include classic RPG text effects: wavy text for mysterious speech, shaking text for loud voices, rainbow gradient for magical words. Color coding for different speakers using restricted palettes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative' container holding dialogue box structure. Box border: Use border-image with 9-slice scaling or composite multiple divs for corners/edges. Main text area: 'p-4 font-mono text-sm leading-relaxed'. Character reveal: Process caption data character by character, appendChild with 10-50ms delays. Bounce effect: Each character wrapped in span with animation: translateY(-2px). Emotion indicators: Separate TextAtom positioned 'absolute -top-4 right-0' with pixel emoji. Menu cursor: Div with 'absolute w-0 h-0' using border triangle trick, animated translateX. Screen shake: Parent container animation with small random translates. Flash: Overlay div with 'absolute inset-0 bg-white pointer-events-none' opacity animation. Portrait container: 'absolute left-2 bottom-2 w-16 h-16' with sprite animation. Wavy text: Each character with different animation-delay for sin wave effect. Rainbow: Background gradient with background-clip: text. Use fitDurationTo: 'children' based on text length. Speaker colors: CSS custom properties switched based on input parameter.

prompts.prompt: Design a demoscene-inspired 8-bit typography preset with mathematical precision and synchronized geometric patterns reminiscent of classic Amiga demos. Text should render with copper bar effects (horizontal gradient bars passing behind text), plasma effects, and geometric shape morphing. Each word acts as a mask for underlying animated patterns: checkerboards, sine waves, or rotating star fields. Implement classic demo effects: infinite zoom/tunnel behind text, rotating 3D wireframe cubes as background elements, sine scroll text distortion. Characters should have individual phase offsets creating wave patterns across words. Add raster bar effects with horizontal lines changing color based on screen position. For emphasis, trigger 'greetings' style scrolling text with elastic bounce physics. Include authentic limitations: fixed palette swaps at specific scanlines, sprite multiplexing effects. All animations must be perfectly synchronized using mathematical functions rather than keyframes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative bg-black overflow-hidden' base. Copper bars: Multiple absolute divs with linear gradients, animated translateY in sync. Text masking: Use mix-blend-mode: screen or CSS mask-image. Plasma effect: Canvas element or CSS gradients with hue-rotate animation. Sine distortion: Each character in separate span, translateY based on sin(time + index * phase). Raster bars: Series of 1px high divs with background colors. Tunnel effect: Radial gradient with animated scale and rotation. Wireframe cubes: SVG elements with stroke only, 3D transforms. Mathematical sync: Use single time variable, derive all animations from math functions. Sprite multiplexing: Reuse same elements with rapid position changes. Greetings scroll: Text in single line, translateX with bounce easing. Palette swaps: CSS custom properties changed via JavaScript at specific intervals. Use requestAnimationFrame for precise timing. Performance: Minimize repaints, use transform only, batch DOM updates. Fixed-point math for pixel-perfect positions. Consider using WebGL shader for complex effects if needed.
